passage: Tutor's note, Hemant. Mridul came in on Thursday and said something I liked: “I notice I open the AI before I try the problem.” He had decided to test himself. He closed it, took a fresh problem like last week's, and tried it cold for fifteen minutes. He got stuck at the second step and saw that he could not remember how to set up the equation, something he had let the tool do all month. He wrote down the gap and set a rule for himself: a fair attempt first, twenty minutes; only then ask for a hint, never the answer. We went over the gap together. Next week he will show me his attempts before asking for help. I told him that noticing this on his own is the harder part.

qa.q: How long did Mridul try the problem without the tool?
qa.a: Mridul tried it cold for fifteen minutes.

qa.q: How does Mridul probably feel on seeing the gap?
qa.a: Mridul probably feels uneasy but honest, and determined to fix it, since he wrote down the gap and set a rule.

qa.q: What could Mridul do to make the rule stick?
qa.a: Mridul could show his attempts to Hemant and note where a hint was needed, since a record keeps the habit honest.

qa.q: How might Hemant see Mridul's self-test?
qa.a: Hemant is encouraged, since noticing the dependence alone is the harder part.

grounding: After noticing he depends on AI, a student closes it, tries a similar problem cold, sees gaps and asks for hints only after a fair attempt.

passage:
Sunday night
Realised something bad today. I've done every chemistry numerical this month with the AI open. Mole concept, all of it. Preeti asked me to explain one and I couldn't even start without typing it in.
So I closed the tab. Took question 14 from the exercise, similar to the ones I'd "done", and tried it cold with a timer. Twenty minutes. I got stuck converting grams to moles, which, apparently, I never actually learned. I just watched it happen.
New rule, written on the inside cover:
1) Try every question alone for at least 15 minutes.
2) If stuck, ask the AI for a HINT, not the solution.
3) Redo it the next day without any help.
Did three more that way. Two done alone, one needed a hint. Slow. But it's mine now.
Sumit

qa.q: Which question did Sumit try cold?
What did Sumit feel on failing to explain the problem to Preeti?
qa.a: Sumit felt uneasy and a little alarmed, realising the tool had been doing the thinking all month.

qa.q: What else could Sumit add to the new rule?
qa.a: Sumit could explain one solved problem aloud to Preeti each week, since teaching it shows quickly whether the idea is really understood.

qa.q: How might Preeti see Sumit's change?
qa.a: Preeti, who saw Sumit stuck, may soon find Sumit able to actually explain the numericals, which helps them both.

grounding: Shows a student noticing dependence on AI, trying a similar problem without it, seeing the gaps, and switching to hints only after a fair attempt.
